title: Avoid eval with dynamically constructed shell text
why: eval reparses expanded data as shell syntax, so data can become commands, redirections, or control operators.
suggestion: Use arrays, positional parameters, case dispatch, or direct command invocation instead of constructing shell syntax.
limitations: Only eval arguments containing parameter or command expansion are reported; fully static single-quoted programs are excluded.
The rule cannot prove whether expanded values are attacker-controlled.
